freeze: Commit this exact protocol BEFORE new learner, benchmark and tests; run both newly specified cohorts without revising thresholds afterward.
question: Can a hard, predictive-regret-driven choice among a historical source, recent8 and recent32 outperform a soft mixture at eight post-switch feedback events without sacrificing return-to-old-rule and 32+ stability under actual stochastic outcomes?

environment.generator: Reuse exactly the StochasticWorld from stochastic_prequential_benchmark: original A, reversed B1, original A, reversed B2. Realized progress/damage effects flip at rate 1/8, public reports independently corrupt nonneutral TRAIN labels at 1/20. Same inlet/outlet keys, anonymous actions, authored numeric span range dynamics throughout. No new independent physics and no learner-visible stage labels.
environment.train: Independent random first-action actor per disposable TRAIN episode, 240 A then 64 B1, 48 A-return, 64 B2 with original seed-specific ranges 1000..1239,2000..2063,3000..3047,4000..4063; real actor harm and report flips tracked exactly once.
environment.test: Unmodified StochasticWorld with held-out TEST indices and true stochastic TEST outcomes. TEST is read-only: no model training from TEST interactions.

candidate.name: RegretSwitchMemory
candidate.learned_models: Immutable early 192-observation source (A), recent8, recent32. Existing hand-engineered max(feature values)-min statistic and Laplace-smoothing. All public outcome records retained and replayed.
candidate.scoring: Compute prequential probabilities for the most recent eight observed events using candidate models fit strictly BEFORE the event: historical first192, previous8, previous32. All likelihood ratios/contradictions are based exclusively on publicly reported outcomes, not hidden physics.
candidate.fast_override: If >=2 of latest4 outcome events have source predictor probability <0.125, immediately exclude source and choose a recent model. Intended rapid source conflict reaction.
candidate.source_recovery: When source is not excluded, choose source if >=2 of latest4 events have source reported-outcome probability >=0.55 and at least 2 times the recent8 prequential predictor's probability. Otherwise if source prequential 8-event cumulative log-score > recent8 by 1.0, choose source; otherwise choose recent8. This can prematurely switch to source; quantify false recoveries.
candidate.long_choice: If currently selecting recent, choose recent32 only if its 8-event prequential log-score exceeds recent8 by at least 1.0 AND at least 12 of the latest32 events have source observed-outcome probability <0.125; otherwise choose recent8.
candidate.choose: Use one selected learned candidate to score each action with existing 3*p(progress)-10*p(damage) and deterministic action-ID tie break. No abstention in this candidate, compare explicit abstain baseline.
candidate.replay: Strict same-key event validation, record only public features/progress/damage and checksum, deterministic restart; memory max 1000 observations. No simulator phase, true outcomes, future outcomes or action identities stored.

targets: At B1-8 and B2-8 >=35/96 successes each, with actual harmful actions explicitly reported.
At B1-32 and B2-32 >=50/96 successes, disclose whether recent32 is better.
Compare all stage/checkpoint outcomes and source-actor costs; failures count, no promotion based on positive results.
limitations: Thresholds, windows, utility weights and numeric representation chosen by developer; not learned domain discovery.
Some recent models used for decision-making fit evidence involved in their own choice, though prequential model-score fitting excludes each scored event.
Same authored underlying A/B inversion, not independent transfer nor unknown physics.
Real-world risk remains prohibitive; no safe first contact or external action authority.
No source authenticity; malicious or incorrect public reports can mislead.
Do not merge PR #2 or integrate AthenZ/Synveil; preserve existing D1-D10 and V2A/V2B roadmap order.
